events.region: Boone; Lake; Ogle; Lee; De Kalb; Kane; DuPage; Kendall; Northern Cook; Central Cook; Southern Cook; Northern Will; Lake; Porter
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of Illinois, including the following areas, Boone,
Central Cook, De Kalb, DuPage, Kane, Kendall, Lake IL, Lee,
Northern Cook, Northern Will, Ogle and Southern Cook and northwest
Indiana, including the following areas, Lake IN and Porter.

* WHEN...Through early Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding
may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Roads and streets may
be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An additional round of showers and thunderstorms, some with very
heavy rainfall, are expected this evening and overnight which may
result in areas of flash flooding, particularly over urban or
areas of poor drainage.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Fillmore, MN; Mower, MN; Olmsted, MN
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Fillmore County in southeastern Minnesota...
Mower County in southeastern Minnesota...
Southern Olmsted County in southeastern Minnesota...

* WHEN...Until 500 PM CDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads remain closed due to flooding. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1030 AM CDT, local law enforcement reported ongoing flooding
across the warned area due to 4 to 8 inches of rainfall that
occurred overnight. Multiple roadways across the region are
closed.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Austin, Preston, Stewartville, Chatfield, Spring Valley,
Rushford, Grand Meadow, Harmony, Mabel, Lanesboro, Brownsdale,
Wykoff, Fountain, Canton, High Forest, Lansing, Rushford Village,
Pleasant Grove, Washington and Highland.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Buchanan; Delaware; Dubuque; Linn; Jones; Jackson; Cedar; Clinton; Muscatine; Scott; Jo Daviess; Stephenson; Carroll; Whiteside; Rock Island
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding and flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest Illinois, including the following
counties, Carroll, Jo Daviess, Rock Island, Stephenson and
Whiteside and Iowa, including the following counties, Buchanan,
Cedar, Clinton, Delaware, Dubuque, Jackson, Jones, Linn, Muscatine
and Scott.

* WHEN...Through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rounds of showers and storms are expected through tonight. These
storms will be capable of rainfall rates between 1 to 2 inches
per hour. Additional rainfall totals of 1 to 3 inches are likely
along I-80 through Highway 20 through early Sunday morning with
the potential for isolated areas of 3+ inches.

events.region: Allegan; Barry; Van Buren; Kalamazoo; Calhoun
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of south central and southwest Michigan, including
the following counties, in south central Michigan, Calhoun. In
southwest Michigan, Allegan, Barry, Kalamazoo and Van Buren.

* WHEN...Through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- 1 to 3 inches of rain has fallen across the Flood Watch area.
Some localized ponding of water has been reported. This afternoon
will bring a lull in the activity, however more rain will spread
in this evening and continue through the night. Precipitation is
expected to taper off Sunday morning. The rain that has fallen
already has saturated the ground and additional rainfall will go
into run off and potential flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
...The National Weather Service in La Crosse has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Minnesota...

South Branch Root River at Lanesboro affecting Fillmore and Houston
Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...South Branch Root River at Lanesboro.

* WHEN...Until Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, The river may begin to threaten "The Flat"
area at this level and the ballfield will begin to experience some
flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 10.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
afternoon to a crest of 15.2 feet this evening. It will then fall
below flood stage just after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 14.2
feet on 06/09/2008.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
